**SECTION A: A Plotting Program (Program Development) (30 marks)**

**Describing the Task.** Many interesting programming problems involving nested loops can be encountered when creating plots using a printer. Your task is to create the plot in Figure 1 (pyramid) in a general manner with the size of the base entered at the beginning of program execution. Arrays are not used to do this. (The grid lines are just to ease working with the figure; the lines are not directly needed to answer any question.) A pyramid has a number of stars at its base (MaxNoOfStars), and is made up of rows of spaces and stars. Each line of the pyramid is made up of an odd number of leading spaces (NoOfSpaces) followed by a number of stars (NoOfStars). There are blanks after the stars, but they are not important for this exercise.

(Figure 1 of the paper shows the pyramid of stars: a base of 11 stars, and above it lines of 9, 7, 5, 3 and 1 stars, each line centred over the one below.)

questions.enonce_markdown: The procedure *Initialise (MaxNoOfStars, NoOfSpaces, NoOfStars)* to initialise the variables *MaxNoOfStars*, *NoOfSpaces* and *NoOfStars* for the first line.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Algorithm (pseudocode)**

```text
PROCEDURE Initialise(MaxNoOfStars, NoOfSpaces, NoOfStars)
    REPEAT
        INPUT base
    UNTIL base is odd AND base >= 1
    MaxNoOfStars <- base
    NoOfSpaces   <- (base - 1) / 2
    NoOfStars    <- 1
END PROCEDURE
```

The three parameters are results of the procedure, so they are passed **by reference** (pointers in C, `var` parameters in Pascal).

**Program (ANSI C)**

```c
void Initialise(int *MaxNoOfStars, int *NoOfSpaces, int *NoOfStars)
{
    int base = 0;

    printf("Enter the size of the base (an odd positive integer): ");
    scanf("%d", &base);
    while (base < 1 || base % 2 == 0)       /* reject even or non-positive values */
    {
        printf("The base must be an odd positive integer. Try again: ");
        scanf("%d", &base);
    }
    *MaxNoOfStars = base;                   /* stars on the last line (the base) */
    *NoOfSpaces = (base - 1) / 2;           /* the first line is centred over the base */
    *NoOfStars = 1;                         /* the first line has a single star */
}
```

The size of the base is read at the start of the execution, as the description requires. The test `base % 2 == 0` rejects even values and `base < 1` rejects zero and negative values; for an accepted value the first line has `(base - 1) / 2` blanks and one star.

Example: with `base = 9` the procedure leaves `MaxNoOfStars = 9`, `NoOfSpaces = 4`, `NoOfStars = 1`.

questions.enonce_markdown: The procedure *OutputLeadingSpaces (nSpaces)* which takes the number *nSpaces* and outputs that number of leading spaces for a line on the screen.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Algorithm**

```text
PROCEDURE OutputLeadingSpaces(nSpaces)
    FOR i <- 1 TO nSpaces DO
        OUTPUT ' ' (no new line)
END PROCEDURE
```

**Program (ANSI C)**

```c
void OutputLeadingSpaces(int nSpaces)
{
    int i;

    for (i = 1; i <= nSpaces; i++)
        putchar(' ');
}
```

`nSpaces` is only read, so it is passed by value. If `nSpaces` is 0 (the base line) the loop body is not executed and nothing is printed. The line is not ended here: the stars follow on the same line.

questions.enonce_markdown: The procedure *OutputLineOfStars (nStars)* which takes the number *nStars* and outputs that number of stars for a line on the screen.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Algorithm**

```text
PROCEDURE OutputLineOfStars(nStars)
    FOR i <- 1 TO nStars DO
        OUTPUT '*' (no new line)
    OUTPUT new line
END PROCEDURE
```

**Program (ANSI C)**

```c
void OutputLineOfStars(int nStars)
{
    int i;

    for (i = 1; i <= nStars; i++)
        putchar('*');
    putchar('\n');                          /* end of the line */
}
```

After the stars the procedure outputs a new line, so that the next call of `OutputLeadingSpaces` starts on a new screen line (this is what produces one row of the pyramid per call).

questions.enonce_markdown: The procedure *Adjust (NoOfSpaces, NoOfStars)* adjusts the variables *NoOfSpaces* and *NoOfStars* to the values used to print the next row of blanks and stars.
questions.corrige_markdown:
From Task 1 (iv): printing from the top, each line has one blank fewer and two stars more than the line above.

**Algorithm**

```text
PROCEDURE Adjust(NoOfSpaces, NoOfStars)
    NoOfSpaces <- NoOfSpaces - 1
    NoOfStars  <- NoOfStars + 2
END PROCEDURE
```

**Program (ANSI C)**

```c
void Adjust(int *NoOfSpaces, int *NoOfStars)
{
    *NoOfSpaces = *NoOfSpaces - 1;          /* one blank less ... */
    *NoOfStars = *NoOfStars + 2;            /* ... and two more stars */
}
```

Both parameters are modified, so they are passed by reference (pointers). Example: from `(NoOfSpaces, NoOfStars) = (5, 1)` the call gives `(4, 3)`; from `(0, 11)` it gives `(-1, 13)`, which is what ends the loop of the main program.
